title: Brand Name Registration for Seafood and Food Businesses in Karunagappally
metaTitle: Seafood & Food Brand Registration in Karunagappally | BRNDNUR
metaDescription: Essential guide for Karunagappally seafood processors, coastal food brands, and cold chains. File Class 29 trademarks and secure FoSCoS licenses.
intendedAudience: Seafood cold storage owners, coastal fish packaging operators, and food brand founders in Karunagappally, Ochira, and Chavara.
quickAnswer: Seafood and food ventures in Karunagappally must register their brand names under Nice Class 29 (for fresh, frozen, dried, and processed fish and crustaceans) to secure exclusive trade rights across domestic and export markets. Concurrently, enterprises must maintain an active FSSAI State or Central License via FoSCoS to comply with food safety packaging mandates.

content: Karunagappally, situated adjacent to the Neendakara-Kayamkulam coastal fisheries belt, is a key hub for marine landings, mechanized boat operations, cold chain facilities, and seafood value-addition. Many coastal enterprises are shifting from bulk dockside trading to branded consumer seafood packs, vacuum-sealed frozen fish, and dried seafood retail lines.

Without a registered trademark, building customer loyalty is precarious. Competitors can easily package inferior catches in similar bags, damaging your market standing and diluting your pricing power.

Class 29 is the statutory classification for all animal-origin foods and seafood under the Trade Marks Act, 1999. In your Form TM-A specification, ensure that you explicitly enumerate your marine product range:
checklist: Processed and Frozen Fish: Marine and freshwater fish fillets, cleaned whole fish, frozen blocks.
Crustaceans and Shellfish: Processed prawns, lobsters, crabs, and squid (not live).
Value-Added Seafood: Fish cutlets, marinated fish steaks, dried and salted fish products.
Wholesale & Retail (Class 35): Operating cold storage retail fish hubs and online home-delivery seafood portals.

h2Sections.h2: FSSAI Packaging Regulations for Packaged Fish
content: Under the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, packaged seafood sold under a commercial brand must strictly display the 14-digit FSSAI license number, net weight, catch date, freezing date, storage instructions (e.g., "Store below -18°C"), and the registered brand name.

callout.title: Brand Registry for D2C Fish Delivery
callout.text: If your Karunagappally enterprise sells direct-to-consumer seafood online or on aggregator platforms, a registered trademark certificate is mandatory to gate your brand and prevent unauthorized third parties from listing under your brand title.

faqs.question: Can I trademark live fish under Class 29?
faqs.answer: No. Live fish, live lobsters, and aquaculture stock fall under Nice Class 31. Class 29 is strictly reserved for dead, processed, or frozen seafood intended for human consumption.

faqs.question: What is the government filing fee for a seafood partnership firm with Udyam?
faqs.answer: A partnership firm holding a valid Udyam MSME certificate qualifies for the subsidized government fee of ₹4,500 per class instead of the corporate fee of ₹9,000.
